reflection.quote: The most regretful people on earth are those who felt the call to creative work, who felt their own creative power restive and uprising, and gave to it neither power nor time.
reflection.reading:
Sunday used to be a write-off. If Saturday night went the way it usually did, Sunday was a slow crawl through shame and sugar, watching the light change through the blinds and negotiating with yourself about when you could reasonably eat, shower, exist. The day was a hostage situation. You'd tell yourself Monday would be different, and sometimes you even meant it.

Sober Sundays are strange at first because they just... happen. You wake up early. The coffee tastes like coffee. You have the whole day, and nobody is going to give you a script for it. That can feel like freedom or like a small kind of terror, depending on the week. Both are honest reactions. What Mary Oliver understood is that time doesn't announce itself. It just passes, and the question of whether you gave it any of your actual power is one you answer with your Sundays as much as your Mondays.

You don't have to make today productive. You don't have to earn it. But you might, quietly, notice that you have it — this full unhungover day — and decide to be somewhere in it. A walk. A phone call you've been putting off. A book. The small work of being a person who shows up for their own life. That's the whole thing, really. That's what got built while you weren't looking.
reflection.meditation: Where am I actually present today, and where am I still just waiting for the day to end?

affirmations: I have a full day in front of me and I am awake for it.
I don't have to earn my sobriety today — I just have to live inside it.
I am becoming someone I can spend a quiet Sunday with.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Sunday that isn't a recovery mission. Grateful for coffee that tastes like coffee, for a clear head, for the ordinary miracle of remembering last night. Grateful for the people who stayed through the years I was hard to love, and for the version of me learning to be easier company — for them and for myself.
gratitude.closing: One more day, awake for it. That's the whole prayer.
